extracted.intended_audience: administrative law practitioners, public commenters, and advocates participating in notice-and-comment rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing public comments on agency rulemakings under APA §553, emphasizing substantive argumentation because courts cannot impose extra procedural requirements. Advises how to make comments effective given Vermont Yankee's holding about procedural limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: APA §553 as procedural ceiling
rubrics_metrics.description: The APA requirements represent the ceiling of mandatory procedures—agencies cannot be required to do more than what the APA specifies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vermont Yankee held that lower courts may not impose procedural requirements on agencies beyond those in the APA. Practitioners should therefore recognize that courts will not order additional procedural protections for commenters beyond §553.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work within the §553 framework (notice, comment, concise general statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must work within the basic §553 framework: notice, opportunity to comment, concise general statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submissions meet timing and form requirements of §553 (respond to the noticed rule, file within the comment period, and provide a concise general statement when required). Preserve a formal administrative record by submitting official comments rather than only informal or peripheral participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on substantive content over procedural demands
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive content matters more than demanding additional process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because courts will not require extra procedures, prioritize solid legal and factual arguments, data, and reasoned alternatives rather than requests for cross-examination, hearings, or other court-enforceable process expansions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on courts to compel additional procedures (no forced cross‑examination/hearings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't expect a court to force agencies to consider comments more carefully than §553 requires; cross-examination, formal hearings, etc. cannot be required by courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid strategies that assume a judge will mandate expanded procedure. Requests for adversarial procedures (e.g., cross-examination) or court-forced additional notice are unlikely to succeed post-Vermont Yankee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use State Farm / hard‑look standards to force substantive responses
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty to respond comes from State Farm/hard‑look doctrine, not from procedural innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft comments to show agency failures in reasoned decisionmaking (e.g., ignored evidence, unexplained departures, inadequate analysis). A strong substantive showing under State Farm is the path to require meaningful agency responses, not procedural complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make comments self‑sufficient and record‑focused
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should be self-sufficient: don't rely on procedural follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete arguments, supporting evidence, and clearly articulated alternatives or changes within the comment itself. Because courts are unlikely to compel further process, your initial submission must contain what you need the agency (or a reviewing court) to consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate terse but legally defensible agency responses
rubrics_metrics.description: The ceiling principle means agency response can be terse if defensible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect agencies to issue concise responses so long as they can show a defensible path. Design comments to make terse rationales insufficient under hard‑look review (e.g., by identifying specific overlooked facts or reasoning gaps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat agency procedural innovations as voluntary
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies' procedural innovations (e.g., online docket discussions) are voluntary and can vary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in novel forums should not substitute for submitting a formal comment under §553. Preserve the official record and do not assume participation in informal or experimental processes creates a judicially enforceable duty to consider your input.
